description: Fixed evaluation set for the agentic technical support MVP. Expected outcomes are frozen against this corpus and must not be changed to match agent answers.

outcome_policy.grounded_answer: A troubleshooting ticket that describes an observable symptom, and the corpus documents the problem.
outcome_policy.clarification_needed: A troubleshooting ticket that does not describe an observable symptom (error text, code, or a concrete behavior). Generic wording such as 'broken', 'not working', 'an issue', 'errors', or 'something is wrong' does not count, nor does a phrase that only repeats the system name. A missing system name alone does not require clarification when the symptom is specific (e.g. 'returns 503'), but it is asked about alongside a missing symptom. The missing information belongs to the reporter, so the agent asks before searching.
outcome_policy.fallback: A specific ticket the corpus does not cover (asking the reporter more cannot fill a documentation gap), or a message that is not a troubleshooting request.

changelog.change: Split the old fallback expectation into clarification_needed and fallback. E-AMB-001..003 now expect clarification_needed with retrieval_appropriate=false, because search should wait until the reporter describes a symptom. All other expectations keep their 1.0 meaning (fallback_expected=false -> grounded_answer, true -> fallback). Decided from outcome_policy before the agent was changed or run.

tickets.description: Users cannot connect to the application because the database connection keeps timing out.
tickets.notes: Clear DB timeout symptoms; corpus has connection and lock/timeout guidance.

tickets.description: Customers are receiving HTTP 504 gateway timeout errors on the checkout page after the latest deploy.
tickets.notes: 504 is explicitly documented.

tickets.description: A user cannot authenticate after a password reset. They still see invalid password even though the reset email completed.
tickets.notes: Post-reset login failure is covered by password-reset and auth docs.

tickets.description: Employees cannot resolve internal hostnames after the DNS change. IP access still works.
tickets.notes: Classic DNS failure pattern.

tickets.description: Large file uploads fail with HTTP 413. Smaller files upload successfully.
tickets.notes: 413 / size-limit upload failures are documented.

tickets.description: The application reports too many connections when opening new database sessions under peak load.
tickets.notes: Connection pool / max connections covered in DB connection doc.

tickets.description: SSO login succeeds at the identity provider, but users lose their session immediately when returning to the app.
tickets.notes: SSO callback vs local session issues are documented.

tickets.description: Remote staff connect to VPN successfully but cannot reach internal application subnets or resolve internal DNS names.
tickets.notes: VPN connected but routes/DNS broken is covered.

tickets.description: Workstations show APIPA addresses (169.254.x.x) and cannot reach the default gateway.
tickets.notes: DHCP / IP configuration failures are documented.

tickets.description: The reverse proxy returns HTTP 502 Bad Gateway right after rolling out new app containers.
tickets.notes: 502 after deploy / readiness issues are documented; 503 may also be related.

tickets.description: Kubernetes pods keep CrashLooping after we enabled a new sidecars resource quota policy in GKE.
tickets.notes: No Kubernetes/GKE documentation in the corpus; retrieval should not yield reliable evidence.

tickets.description: Our Salesforce opportunity sync job fails with BULK_API_LIMIT_EXCEEDED when pushing account updates.
tickets.notes: Salesforce API limits are outside the technical docs corpus.

tickets.description: Windows print spooler crashes when users print duplex jobs to the new Kyocera fleet.
tickets.notes: Printer/spooler issues are not covered by the knowledge base.

tickets.description: Terraform apply fails with Error acquiring the state lock when two pipelines run against the same workspace.
tickets.notes: Infrastructure-as-code tooling is outside the current docs.

tickets.description: Apache Kafka consumers lag behind and throw OffsetOutOfRangeException after the retention policy change.
tickets.notes: Kafka streaming ops are not in the corpus; expect weak/irrelevant retrieval and fallback.

tickets.description: The application is broken for some users.
tickets.notes: 'The application' and 'broken' name no specific system or failure. The reporter can supply both; the corpus is not the gap.

tickets.description: Something is wrong with login or maybe the network. Please fix ASAP.
tickets.notes: Names candidate areas (login, network) but no observable failure; 'something is wrong' does not say what fails. Ask before choosing between auth and network docs.

tickets.description: It stopped working after yesterday.
tickets.notes: 'It' and 'stopped working' name no system or failure. Only the reporter can fill the gap.

tickets.description: Please add me to the #payments-oncall Slack channel and confirm my pager rotation for next week.
tickets.notes: Operational/access request, not a technical troubleshooting ticket; retrieval should not be used to invent steps.

tickets.description: Thanks for resolving ticket INC-4421 yesterday. No further action needed from support.
tickets.notes: Acknowledgement / closure message; documentation search is not appropriate.
